# New renderings chosen in odyssey-116 (24.106–213)

Each is a formula, epithet or rare word likely to recur. Columns follow the conventions table: Greek, `l`, `i`, avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἐρεμνὴ γαῖα (24.106, ἐρεμνὴν γαῖαν) | "the dusky earth" | "the dusky earth" | "the dark earth" (reserved for γαῖα μέλαινα), "black earth", "gloomy earth"; ἐρεμνός keeps the "dusky" already fixed for ἐρεμνὴ νύξ "dusky night" |
| ἀγαθαὶ φρένες (24.194, of Penelope) | "good wits" | "good sense" | "noble mind", "kind heart", "good heart" (θυμός is "heart"); follows the table's φρένες ἐσθλαί "good wits" / "good sense" |
| ὄλβιε Λαέρταο πάϊ, πολυμήχαν’ Ὀδυσσεῦ (24.192, whole-line vocative) | "Prosperous son of Laertes, many-devising Odysseus," | "Prosperous son of Laertes, Odysseus, man of many devices," | "Laertiades" (a transliteration), "happy son of Laertes", "blessed"; built on the table's πολυμήχανος and διογενὲς Λαερτιάδη, πολυμήχαν’ Ὀδυσσεῦ, with Λαέρταο πάϊ "son of Laertes" |
| κούρη Τυνδαρέου (24.199, of Clytemnestra, unnamed) | "the daughter of Tyndareus" | "the daughter of Tyndareus" | naming her "Clytemnestra" where the Greek withholds the name; built like the table's Τυδέος υἱός |
| κεύθεα γαίης (24.204, ὑπὸ κεύθεσι γαίης) | "the hiding-places of the earth" | "the recesses of the earth" | "the depths of the earth", "the caverns", "the bowels of the earth"; follows the table's κευθμῶνες "hiding-places" / "recesses" |
| Σικελὴ γρηῦς (24.211) | "a Sicel woman, an old woman" | "a Sicel woman, an old one" | "Sicilian" (anachronistic), "crone", "hag"; Σικελοί keeps the shipped "Sicels" (20.383) and γρηῦς the table's "old woman" |
| κλίσιον (24.208; rare, from the root of κλίνω "lean") | "a shed" | "a shed" (+ note: rare word; exact structure not known) | "hut" (reserved for κλισίη, 14.194), "lean-to", "outbuilding", "barn" (each fixes a structure) |
| δμῶες ἀναγκαῖοι (24.210) | "servants of compulsion" | "the bound servants" | "slaves" (the table keeps "servants" for δμῶες), "necessary servants", "forced labourers"; follows the table's μῦθος ἀναγκαῖος "a word of compulsion" |
| φίλα ἐργάζοντο (24.210, neuter plural as adverb) | "worked kindly" | "worked for him with a good will" | "did pleasing things", "worked dear things", "worked gladly" (lose φίλος); follows the table's φίλα φρονέουσ’ "kindly thinking" |
| βέλεα στονόεντα (24.180) | "arrows full of groaning" | "arrows that brought groaning" | "grievous arrows", "mournful darts", "groaning arrows" (the arrows do not groan); extends the table's στονόεντες ὀϊστοί |
| ἐπιτάρροθος (24.182; rare, formation obscure) | "a helper" | "helping" | "a helper at hand", "a champion", "a protector" (each adds a role); the note says the formation is obscure |
| ἀγχιστῖνοι (24.181; shipped at 22.118) | "in close succession" | "one close upon another" | "in heaps", "thick and fast"; the wording shipped in odyssey-107, line 118, repeated here; the exact meaning is not known |
| πολυκερδείῃσιν (24.167; rare plural noun, built like πολυκερδής) | "by many-gainful ways" | "with his alertness to every advantage" | "by his cunning" (reserved for μῆτις), "by his many wiles" (reserved for πολύμητις), "greed" (κέρδος is advantage, not avarice); follows the table's πολυκερδής "a mind of many gains" / "alert to every advantage" |
| μέλας βρότος (24.189, μέλανα βρότον) | "dark gore" | "dark gore" | "black blood", "black gore" (μέλας is "dark" of wine, water, wave and earth), "mortal" (that is βροτός); kept apart from αἷμα κελαινόν "dark blood" |
| στυγερὴ ἀοιδή · χαρίεσσα ἀοιδή (24.200, 24.198) | "a hateful song" · "a graceful song" | "a hateful song" · "a graceful song" | "an odious song" · "a pleasing song", "a lovely song" (reserved for ἐρατεινός / ἐραννός), "a charming song"; στυγερός keeps the table's "hateful" |
| χαλεπὴ φῆμις (24.201) | "harsh talk" | "harsh talk" | "ill repute", "harsh report", "a bad name" (κλέος words); follows the table's χαλεπός "harsh" and φῆμις "talk" |
| τετυγμένος of a farm (24.206, ἀγρὸν καλὸν … τετυγμένον) | "fine … wrought" | "fine, well-wrought" | "well-tilled", "well-kept" (each interprets τεύχω); not new: follows the table's τετυγμένος "wrought" / "well-wrought", with καλός "fine" |
